question.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{2}x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{2}x)
$$

Let $F(x)=x+1$ for $x\in [-2,2).$ The Fourier series of the $4$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${a}_{2}.$

${a}_{2}=$ {{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the cosine coefficients are given by

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{L}x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=2$ and $f(x)=x+1$ for $x\in [-2,2).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-2}^{2}(x+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{2}x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-2}^{2}(x+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x+1\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x)\, & ⇒\,v=\frac{1}{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(uv\,{|}_{-2}^{2}-{\int }_{-2}^{2}v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{\pi }{[(x+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)]}_{-2}^{2}-{\int }_{-2}^{2}\frac{1}{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{\pi }[3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )-(-1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(-2\pi )]-\frac{1}{\pi }\cdot (-\frac{1}{\pi }){[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi x)]}_{-2}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{\pi }\cdot 0+\frac{1}{{\pi }^{2}}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(-2\pi )]) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{{\pi }^{2}}(1-1) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
